static_traits.name: Yang Peitong
static_traits.family_status: Lives with mother, close relationship, able to communicate with her when in difficulty
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; without prior similar psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to concretely describe triggering situations and automatic thoughts; fairly good cooperation; somewhat negative tone, accompanied by guilt and self-criticism

basic_info.main_problem: I feel that I am wasting my time on hobbies such as going to concerts and collecting stamps. This view leads me to feel guilt and self-criticism.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of guilt and self-criticism have begun to affect my mood and my enjoyment of important activities.
growth_experiences: About six months ago, a conversation with a friend had a significant impact: the friend criticized her hobbies as 'unproductive' and mocked stamp collecting as 'something only old people do'. Since then, whenever preparing to go to concerts or do stamp collecting on weekends, strong guilt and self-criticism arise, and it has become increasingly hard to find joy in her hobbies.
Close relationship with mother, living together. She communicates with mother when in difficulty, but feels 'not yet understood' on this issue, so emotional relief is limited.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether I am doing something 'useful/productive'
Enjoyment and leisure equal wasting time

special_situations.event: Preparing to attend a concert on the weekend or actually attending a concert
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If something cannot directly improve the future or produce clear output, then it has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to dissuade herself from participating or rationally persuading herself not to go, to avoid guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am wasting time; I should be doing something more meaningful

special_situations.event: Recalls a friend's criticism of my hobby, or talks about the topic of 'whether it is productive'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' evaluations determine whether my behavior has value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Restraining herself through self-criticism, repressing interests to meet others' standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She thinks I am not ambitious enough, so I must be idling about

special_situations.event: When stamp collecting, only noticing its 'no real output' side
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an activity has no visible results or efficiency, it equals waste
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries rationally listing pros and cons, but repeatedly focuses on negative evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These activities are of no use at all

special_situations.event: Recalling past concerts and leisure experiences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If something is deemed 'not useful enough' once, then all such activities are a waste
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling myself as 'wasting time' to force myself to change behavior

core_conflict.wish: Longs, while being recognized by others as 'valuable/productive', to still enjoy personal interests and relaxation at ease
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as 'idle/useless', thus being negated or looked down upon
defense_goal: Avoiding blame through self-criticism and repressing interests
Discussing 'productivity/value' in rationalized terms to reduce anxiety when negated

object_relations.self_representation: An uneasy self needing to prove herself with 'usefulness/productivity'
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are critical and judgmental (friends/outside world)

object_relations.self_representation: A self longing to be understood yet feeling helpless

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others question the 'productivity' of their hobby, or the counseling situation focuses on value/efficiency
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person is negating me; if I enjoy my hobbies I will be looked down upon
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Talks about 'efficiency/output' using objective analysis and data-based language, downplays emotional wording, tone is restrained and organized, avoiding going into subjective feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Strong guilt and self-blame arising when preparing to engage in hobbies near the weekend
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I go enjoy my hobbies, I will fail or be seen as unambitious
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using harsh, self-deprecating statements (e.g. 'I am wasting time'), in a stern tone, proactively giving up or reducing hobby activities to relieve anxiety.

manifestations: Starting to question the value of hobbies, seeing concerts and stamp collecting as 'meaningless/unproductive'
Finds it hard to acknowledge the value of pleasure and relaxation themselves, doubting their meaning in life
outcomes: Anhedonia and reduced interest (no longer enjoying previously liked activities)
Low mood and decreased sense of self-worth

manifestations: Feeling conflicted between 'freely enjoying' and 'being productive responsibly toward oneself'
After internalizing others' standards, space for self-choice is compressed
outcomes: Suppressing interests through self-reproach, leading to psychological tension and internal friction

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly judging herself with 'I should do meaningful things'
Friends' criticism replays repeatedly in the mind and is treated as the standard for judging oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism, worrying whether hobbies are 'useful'
Clearly cautious when talking about hobbies, tending to use self-blame to restrain behavior

positive_force: Fairly close relationship with mother, with basic emotional support resources
Able to sense that activities such as concerts once brought relaxation and happiness (has memories of positive experiences)
Proactively seeks help and is willing to try counseling and cognitive testing (reality testing)
Having a certain rational analysis ability, able to try to evaluate the pros and cons of activities
negative_force: Internalizes the external 'productivity' standard as the criterion for self-worth evaluation, relying on external evaluation
Cognitive biases such as black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and mental filtering reinforce guilt
Strong 'should' beliefs leading to self-harshness and avoidance of enjoyment
The friend's negative evaluations repeatedly trigger guilt and self-denial, ruining the joy of activities

target_behavior.behavior: Strong guilt and self-criticism appear when engaging in hobbies (concerts, stamp collecting), and she tends to reduce or avoid related activities
antecedent: On weekends or when about to do a hobby
Recalling the friend's criticism about 'lack of productivity'
When talking with others about whether to take up hobbies
target_behavior.core_reason: Using 'whether it produces output / is useful' as the sole standard of worth, triggered by the friend's criticism and internalized as a self-evaluation criterion
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncomfortable emotions like guilt and avoiding others' negative evaluations
target_behavior.consequence: Losing interest and joy in previously enjoyable activities, low mood, decreased quality of life
